literal: Longzhi devoted himself to comforting and soothing; the people's hearts were moved to joy.
idiomatic: Longzhi poured himself into comfort and reassurance, and the people warmed to him.

literal: Soon the Grand Ancestor marched east from Jinyang; Longzhi sent his son Zihui to welcome him at Fakou, and the Grand Ancestor greatly praised it.
idiomatic: Soon Gao Huan marched east from Jinyang; Longzhi sent his son Zihui to welcome him at Fakou, and the Grand Ancestor was much pleased.

literal: Having reached Xindu, he gathered the commanders, generals, and officials of the various provinces and commanderies and said: "The rebellious barbarian Erzhu Zhao is utterly ruthless and savage — what Heaven and Earth cannot bear, what gods and men alike cast aside. Rebellions rise everywhere; this is the hour Heaven decrees his fall.
idiomatic: When they reached Xindu, he assembled the provincial commanders, generals, and officials and said, "The rebel Erzhu Zhao is utterly merciless — what Heaven and Earth cannot abide, what gods and men alike reject. Uprisings blaze everywhere; this is the hour of Heaven's judgment.

literal: I wish to join with you all in cutting down these barbarian destroyers — what plan shall we adopt?
idiomatic: I mean to join you in cutting down these villains — what shall our plan be?

literal: Longzhi replied: "The Erzhu are cruel and savage; Heaven's doom draws near. Gods are angry, the people resentful, followers desert and kin turn away — though they hold great armies, their strength may easily become weakness.
idiomatic: Longzhi answered, "The Erzhu rule with savage cruelty; Heaven's judgment is at hand. The gods are wrathful, the people embittered, allies flee and kin forsake them — though they command great armies, strength can turn to weakness in a breath.

literal: Yet Your Highness holds the royal house in your heart and first raised the banner of righteousness — among all under Heaven, who would not look up to you?
idiomatic: Yet Your Highness holds the throne in your heart and first raised the righteous banner — who under Heaven would not rally to you?

literal: I beg Your Highness not to doubt.
idiomatic: I beg Your Highness — do not hesitate.

literal: At the start of Zhongxing he was appointed Left Grand Master of Glorious Affairs and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: At the start of Zhongxing he was appointed left grand master of glorious affairs and minister of personnel.

literal: Erzhu Zhao and others encamped at Guang'a; in the tenth month the Grand Ancestor fought them and routed them utterly.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao and his followers encamped at Guang'a; in the tenth month Gao Huan met them in battle and crushed them.

literal: He then dispatched Longzhi, bearer of the staff, as envoy of the Northern Route.
idiomatic: He then sent Longzhi, bearing the staff of authority, as envoy of the northern route.

literal: The Grand Ancestor was about to strike Erzhu Zhao's army at Hanling and left Longzhi to hold Ye.
idiomatic: As Gao Huan prepared to strike Erzhu Zhao at Hanling, he left Longzhi to hold Ye.

literal: Erzhu Zhao and the rest fled; Longzhi was made to act in Ji Province affairs and still took charge of more than thirty thousand surrendered captives, distributing them among the provinces.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao and the rest fled; Longzhi was put in charge of Ji Province and given more than thirty thousand surrendered captives to settle among the provinces.

literal: Soon he was recalled as Attending Internuncio.
idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to court as attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: At that time the Grand Ancestor returned from Luoyang with his army to Ye.
idiomatic: At that time Gao Huan brought his army back from Luoyang to Ye.

literal: Longzhi was about to go to the capital; on the way he paid a call and reported to the Grand Ancestor: "Husi Chun, Helü Sheng, and Jia Xianzhi once served the Erzhu, then turned and obstructed you; when you campaigned against Zhongyuan, they sided with him again — men cruel and suspicious, whose ambitions know no bound.
idiomatic: Longzhi was bound for the capital; stopping to pay his respects, he warned the Grand Ancestor, "Husi Chun, Helü Sheng, and Jia Xianzhi once served the Erzhu, then turned against you; when you marched against Zhongyuan they sided with him again — cruel, suspicious men whose greed knows no limit.

literal: Also Chi Lie, Yanqing, and Hou.
idiomatic: Then there are Chi Lie, Yanqing, and Hou—

literal: Nianxian are all in the capital; Your Highness has granted them rank and office — such men will surely sow the seeds of disaster.
idiomatic: Nianxian, all of them in the capital. Your Highness has given them rank and office; men like these will surely brew trouble.

literal: After a night had passed the Grand Ancestor said to Longzhi: "What the Attending Internuncio said yesterday was truly far-sighted counsel.
idiomatic: After a night's sleep the Grand Ancestor told Longzhi, "Your words yesterday were counsel of true foresight.

literal: Soon he was enfeoffed Duke of Ande Commandery with a fief of two thousand households, and advanced to honor equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Soon he was enfeoffed duke of Ande Commandery with a fief of two thousand households and promoted to rank equal to the three excellencies.

literal: At that time court discussion held that since Erzhu Rong had aided the mandate in the previous dynasty, he should receive temple sacrifice alongside Emperor Ming in the ancestral hall.
idiomatic: The court then debated whether Erzhu Rong, who had helped establish the previous reign, ought to receive sacrifice in Emperor Ming's temple hall.

literal: Longzhi argued: "Rong was a subject who himself carried out regicide — how could we place the mother he murdered facing her son at the same feast?
idiomatic: Longzhi objected, "Rong was a subject who slew his sovereign with his own hand — what sense is there in seating the mother he murdered opposite her son at the same table?"

literal: Searching antiquity and inquiring of the present, I see no precedent for such a thing.
idiomatic: Search antiquity, consult the present — nowhere do I find precedent for such a thing.

literal: The court accepted his view.
idiomatic: The court agreed.

literal: An edict ordered Longzhi to join deliberations at the Linqi Pavilion to fix the new regulations.
idiomatic: An edict appointed Longzhi to deliberations at the Linqi Pavilion to establish the new code.

literal: His wife, née Zu, was also posthumously granted Lady of Fanyang Commandery.
idiomatic: His wife, Lady Zu, was also granted the title Lady of Fanyang Commandery.

literal: Longzhi memorialized that his earlier ranks of Baron of Fucheng and Baron of Wucheng should be transferred to his nephews Xiaowan and others; the court praised this and agreed.
idiomatic: Longzhi petitioned to transfer his earlier baronies of Fucheng and Wucheng to his nephews Xiaowan and the others; the court approved and praised his generosity.

literal: Later Husi Chun and others slandered him to the Wei emperor, and he fled home to his native district.
idiomatic: Later Husi Chun and his faction framed him before the Wei emperor, and he fled to his home district.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, knowing he had been falsely accused, summoned him to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Knowing he had been slandered, Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang.

literal: The Wei emperor soon recalled him at his former rank, but Longzhi firmly declined and did not go.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor soon recalled him to his former post; Longzhi steadfastly refused.

literal: Longzhi was instead made to act as Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: Longzhi was instead put in charge of Bing Province.

literal: Prince Qinghe Dan of Wei served as Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: Prince Qinghe Dan of Wei was grand marshal.

literal: Chief Administrator.
idiomatic: Longzhi served as his chief administrator.

literal: At the start of Tianping he returned as Attending Internuncio and took part in deliberations over moving the capital.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianping he returned as attendant-in-ordinary and joined deliberations on moving the capital.

literal: Emperor Jing of Wei ordered him Lecturer-in-Attendance, appointed him Minister of Personnel, added Attending Internuncio, and had him act in Ji Province affairs at his present rank.
idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Wei named him lecturer-in-attendance, appointed him minister of personnel and attendant-in-ordinary, and charged him with Ji Province affairs while keeping his existing rank.

literal: Lu Shaozun of Yangping gathered a crowd in rebellion, styled himself Mobile Imperial Secretariat, broke Ding Province's Boling Commandery, captured the administrator Gao Yongle, and invaded Ji Province from the south.
idiomatic: Lu Shaozun of Yangping raised a rebel band, styled himself mobile imperial secretariat, overran Boling in Ding Province, seized the prefect Gao Yongle, and pushed south into Ji Province.

literal: Longzhi ordered Gao Jing, Administrator of Changle under his command, and others to break them; Shaozun was captured alive and sent to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Longzhi ordered Gao Jing, prefect of Changle, and others to defeat them, took Shaozun alive, and sent him to Jinyang.

literal: At the start of Yuanxiang he was appointed Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: At the start of Yuanxiang he was appointed governor of Ji Province.

literal: Soon the seal of opening an office was added.
idiomatic: Soon he was given the seal of opening an office.

literal: At that time, when brave fighters were first being conscripted, the commanders Bo Ba, Gao Faxiong, and Feng Ziyuan and others, unwilling to serve far from home, gathered crowds and rebelled.
idiomatic: When fresh conscripts of proven courage were first being mustered, commanders Bo Ba, Gao Faxiong, and Feng Ziyuan and others, unwilling to garrison far away, rose in armed revolt.

literal: Longzhi led the provincial army, broke them, and pacified them.
idiomatic: Longzhi led the provincial troops, broke them, and restored order.

literal: In the first year of Xinghe he was again recalled as Attending Internuncio.
idiomatic: In the first year of Xinghe he was recalled once more to court as attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: Longzhi had long won the hearts of his home district; having served his native province again and again, he cared for the people in word and deed — officials and commoners remembered him and set up steles praising his virtue.
idiomatic: Longzhi had always held the affection of his home country; serving his native province again and again, he governed with genuine care — when he left, officials and commoners raised steles in his praise.

literal: He was transferred to act in Liang Province affairs, then again to act in Ji Province affairs, and recalled as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He acted in turn for Liang Province and Ji Province, then was recalled as right vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: At the start of Wuding, Gao Zhongmi, Governor of Northern Yu Province, was about to rebel; he secretly sent envoys to the magnates of Ji Province, seeking inside cooperation.
idiomatic: At the start of Wuding, Gao Zhongmi, governor of Northern Yu Province, prepared to rebel; he sent secret envoys to Ji Province's great families to arrange inside support.

literal: Frivolous elements stirred one another to agitation; an edict sent Longzhi by relay post to comfort and soothe, and calm was restored.
idiomatic: Restless elements stirred one another toward revolt; an edict dispatched Longzhi by relay horse to reassure the region, and order returned.

literal: Shizong wrote secretly to Longzhi: "Among Zhongmi's partisans and fellow wrongdoers who fled west, their families should all be seized, to warn those who come after.
idiomatic: Shizong wrote privately to Longzhi, "Of Zhongmi's partisans and fellow conspirators who fled west, seize all their families — let that be a warning to those who come after."

literal: Longzhi held that once clemency had been proclaimed, reason forbade reversing it; to seize people now would show the people that the court's word could not be trusted — and if alarm and unrest followed, the loss would be great.
idiomatic: Longzhi argued that clemency once proclaimed could not be revoked without cost; to round people up now would teach the populace that the throne's word meant nothing — and if panic spread, the damage would far outweigh the gain.

literal: He reported to the Grand Ancestor, and the matter was halted.
idiomatic: He appealed to Gao Huan, and the order was withdrawn.

literal: From the first raising of the righteous banner Longzhi took part in planning; his ingenious stratagems were reported in secret memorials — he wrote by hand and erased his drafts, and few outside knew of them.
idiomatic: From the moment the righteous banner first rose, Longzhi shared in every plan; his keenest stratagems he reported only in secret — writing by hand and burning the drafts, so that few beyond the inner circle ever knew.

literal: The Grand Ancestor praised his loyalty and prudence and often followed his counsel.
idiomatic: Gao Huan valued his loyalty and discretion and often took his advice.

literal: Again acting in Ji Province affairs at his present rank, he was transferred to Governor of Qi Province; in the third year of Wuding he died in office, aged sixty-one.
idiomatic: He again acted for Ji Province, then was transferred to governor of Qi Province; in the third year of Wuding he died in office, aged sixty-one.

literal: An edict sent Director of the Masters of Documents Shen Gui to offer condolences on the spot, with five hundred bolts of condolence goods; posthumously granted bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Cang and Ying provinces, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Governor of Ying Province, and Duke over the Masses.
idiomatic: The court sent Director Shen Gui with five hundred bolts of burial goods; posthumously Longzhi was granted bearer of the staff, military command over Cang and Ying provinces, grand general of fast cavalry, governor of Ying Province, and duke over the masses.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, considering Longzhi's long service and merit and that posthumous honors had not yet been fully bestowed, again petitioned: posthumously grant bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ying, Cang, Qi, and Jizhou, Governor of Ji Province, and Grand Guardian — all else as before; posthumous title Xuanyi.
idiomatic: Believing Longzhi's honors still fell short of his service, Gao Huan petitioned again: posthumously grant him bearer of the staff, military command over Ji, Ying, Cang, Qi, and Jizhou provinces, governorship of Ji Province, and grand guardian, with other titles unchanged; posthumous name Xuanyi, "Sincere and Restrained."

literal: Later the Grand Ancestor reached Ji Province's border and halted at Jiaojin.
idiomatic: Later, passing through Ji Province, Gao Huan halted at Jiaojin.

literal: Recalling Longzhi, he turned and said to Si Maziru, acting chief of Ji Province affairs: "Lord Feng accumulated virtue and practiced benevolence; his nature was penetrating and his understanding thorough. From the day he entered the management of army and state, nearly twenty years — through hardship and trial, from first to last he was one and the same.
idiomatic: Thinking of Longzhi, he turned to Si Maziru, acting chief of Ji Province, and said, "Lord Feng heaped up merit and walked in benevolence; he understood men and grasped affairs. For nearly twenty years he governed army and state — through every hardship, unchanged to the end.

literal: Because his loyalty and trustworthiness could be relied upon, I was just about to entrust the affairs that come after to him.
idiomatic: I trusted his loyalty and meant to entrust my legacy to him.

literal: Who expected that reward for good would find no sign — that he would suddenly pass from this life? To speak of such loyalty and worth — how deeply one must grieve.
idiomatic: Who could have foreseen that virtue would go unrewarded — that he would leave us so suddenly? To think on such loyalty and talent is heartbreaking.

literal: He wept for him.
idiomatic: He wept.

literal: He ordered Military Aide Zhong Xian to go with the grand offering and perform sacrifice.
idiomatic: He ordered Military Aide Zhong Xian to go and offer the grand sacrifice.

literal: His eldest son died early.
idiomatic: His eldest son had died young.

literal: The second son, Zihui, succeeded.
idiomatic: His second son Zihui succeeded him.

literal: Zihui, styled Zhongzao, pet name Sao — his nature was harmonious and orderly, and he possessed breadth of vision.
idiomatic: Zihui, styled Zhongzao — pet name Sao — was even-tempered and broad-minded, a man of real capacity.

literal: Upon first taking office he was made Gentleman of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He first entered service as gentleman of the palace secretariat.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao killed Emperor Zhuang of Wei, he and his father Longzhi raised righteousness at Xindu and he was sent as envoy to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao murdered Emperor Zhuang of Wei, he and his father Longzhi raised the righteous banner at Xindu, and Zihui was dispatched as envoy to Gao Huan.

literal: When he reached Xindu he was summoned and appointed Opening-Establishment Chief Clerk, and still superintended the written records.
idiomatic: Arriving at Xindu, he was appointed chief clerk of the opening-establishment office and put in charge of correspondence.

literal: In the first year of Zhongxing he was transferred to chief clerk of the Grand Chancellor and given the rank General Who Quells the Waves.
idiomatic: In Zhongxing 1 he became chief clerk to the grand chancellor and was given the rank general who quells the waves.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in campaigning against Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan against Erzhu Zhao.

literal: When Zhongshan was pacified and the army returned, he was appointed General of Unwavering Integrity and Regular Attendant, Left General, and put in charge of Secretarial Drafting Attendants.
idiomatic: After Zhongshan was pacified and the army returned, he was made general of unwavering integrity and regular attendant, left general, and supervising drafting attendant.

literal: Upon his mother's death he left office for mourning; soon he resumed his former post.
idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother, then soon returned to his former post.

literal: During Taichang he followed the Grand Ancestor in securing several provinces including Bing, Fen, and Si, and in pacifying Erzhu Zhao and the Mountain Hu; he was given the additional ranks General Who Punishes the South and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon. At the end of Emperor Wu of Wei's reign, Husi Chun and other favorites held power; his father Longzhi, fearing trouble from suspicion, secretly returned to his native district — Zihui also left office and returned with him.
idiomatic: In Taichang he followed Gao Huan in securing Bing, Fen, Si, and other provinces and in crushing Erzhu Zhao and the Mountain Hu; he was promoted to general who punishes the south and grand master with the golden seal and purple ribbon. When Emperor Wu of Wei's reign drew to its end, Husi Chun and other favorites held sway; fearing their malice, his father Longzhi slipped away to their home country — and Zihui resigned and went with him.

literal: At the start of Xiaojing's reign he was additionally made Drafting Attendant at the Yellow Gate, and together with Court Director of Ceremonial Li Yuanzhong and others went out bearing the staff on mission to observe local customs and ask after the people's hardships.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he became drafting attendant at the yellow gate and, together with Court Director Li Yuanzhong and others, went abroad bearing the staff to inspect local customs and hear the people's griefs.

literal: On his return he went to Jinyang and followed the Grand Ancestor in campaigning against Xia Province.
idiomatic: Returning, he went to Jinyang and followed Gao Huan against Xia Province.

literal: In the second year he was appointed General of the Guard and Administrator of Pingyang; soon Regular Cavalry Attendant was added.
idiomatic: In the second year he was made general of the guard and prefect of Pingyang; soon he was also named attendant cavalry-in-ordinary.

literal: On Jin Province's northern border stands Mount Huo of Tai — the old route called the Thousand-Li Pass runs over steep ridges; whenever great armies passed, men and horses were worn with toil. Zihui reported to the Grand Ancestor and asked that a separate road be opened through the eastern valley of the old pass.
idiomatic: On Jin Province's northern marches stands the Tai range of Mount Huo — along the old route called the Thousand-Li Pass the slopes are sheer, and every march of a great army left men and horses spent. Zihui petitioned Gao Huan to cut a new road through the eastern valley.

literal: The Grand Ancestor agreed and ordered Zihui to command corvée labor from Fen and Jin provinces for the work; in ten days it was finished.
idiomatic: Gao Huan agreed and put Zihui in charge of corvée from Fen and Jin provinces; within ten days the road was done.

literal: The Grand Ancestor personally commanded the six armies; passing by the new road, he praised its economy and convenience and granted two hundred hu of grain.
idiomatic: Gao Huan personally led the six armies; traveling the new road, he praised its efficiency and rewarded Zihui with two hundred hu of grain.

literal: Later, when the great army recovered Eastern Yong and pacified Chaiyu, Qiaoshan, Zigud, Jiangshu, and the rest, Zihui constantly rode ahead as prefect to comfort the troops and levy men and transport grain — the soldiers wanted for nothing.
idiomatic: When the main force recaptured Eastern Yong and pacified Chaiyu, Qiaoshan, Zigud, Jiangshu, and the rest, Zihui always rode ahead as prefect to hearten the men, levy troops, and move grain — the army never went wanting.

literal: At the start of Xinghe he was recalled from the prefecture and appointed Gentleman-Inspector in the Ministry of Personnel within the Grand Mobile Secretariat.
idiomatic: At the start of Xinghe he was recalled from his prefecture to serve as gentleman-inspector in the personnel office of the grand mobile secretariat.

literal: In the first year of Wuding, Gao Zhongmi rebelled westward from Wulao; Zhou Emperor Wen led a host east in invasion; the Grand Ancestor broke them at Mang Mountain, pursued at full speed while the victory held, and reached Tong Pass.
idiomatic: In Wuding 1, Gao Zhongmi rebelled from Wulao in the west; Yuwen Tai marched east at the head of a great army; Gao Huan routed him at Mang Mountain, pressed the victory hard, and drove all the way to Tong Pass.

literal: Some counseled that he must not pursue war to its utmost extreme; the Grand Ancestor gathered the officials to debate advance or withdrawal.
idiomatic: Some warned against pushing war to its extreme; Gao Huan assembled his ministers to debate whether to advance or withdraw.

literal: Zihui said: "The rebel leader's talent falls short of a true hero; he stole a title and dared to drive fugitive traitors — and perished on the Yi and Chan rivers. Heaven's way punishes excess; in a single morning his host dissolved.
idiomatic: Zihui spoke: "The rebel chieftain is no true champion — he stole a name and dared drive a rabble of deserters to their deaths on the Yi and Chan. Heaven punishes depravity; in one morning his host was dust.

literal: Though he barely escaped with his life, his spirit and courage were both lost.
idiomatic: Though he barely escaped alive, his spirit was shattered.

literal: To unify chariots and script under one rule — the moment is now; what Heaven bestows and one does not take, one will instead be punished for.
idiomatic: To unite all under one rule — the hour is now. Refuse Heaven's gift and you answer for it.

literal: The opportune moment is hard to meet and easy to lose.
idiomatic: Such a moment comes rarely and vanishes quickly.

literal: Long ago when Emperor Wu of Wei pacified Hanzhong, he did not seize Bashu while victory held — hesitation was his error, and regret came too late.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Wei took Hanzhong, he failed to seize Bashu while the triumph held — hesitation was the fault, and regret came too late.

literal: I bow and beg Your Highness not to doubt.
idiomatic: I beg Your Highness — do not hesitate.

literal: The Grand Ancestor was deeply convinced.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was deeply persuaded.

literal: But since the season was already peak summer and he was already forming other plans, he ordered withdrawal.
idiomatic: But summer was at its height and he already nursed other designs — he ordered the army home.

literal: In the third year, upon his father's death he left office.
idiomatic: In the third year he left office to mourn his father.

literal: In the fourth year, when the Grand Ancestor campaigned west, he was recalled as Grand Commander, led Ji Province troops to Ye, followed the Grand Ancestor from Fakou west toward Jin Province, and joined the main army at Yubi.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Gao Huan marched west, Zihui was recalled as grand commander, led Ji Province troops to Ye, followed him from Fakou toward Jin Province, and joined the main force at Yubi.

literal: Zihui was again made Gentleman-Inspector in the Ministry of Personnel within the Grand Mobile Secretariat.
idiomatic: Zihui was again appointed to the personnel office of the grand mobile secretariat.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor's illness grew critical, the army returned to Jinyang; Zihui was brought into the inner chamber, received secret commands face to face, and was charged to go to Shandong to comfort the provinces and commanderies.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan fell mortally ill and the army returned to Jinyang, Zihui was summoned to the inner chamber, received secret orders face to face, and sent to Shandong to steady the provinces.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor died, the death was kept secret and mourning not proclaimed; Shizong made Zihui Administrator of Bohai and ordered him to ride relay post to his post.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan died, the death was kept secret; Shizong appointed Zihui prefect of Bohai and dispatched him by relay horse to take up the post.

literal: Shizong personally took his hand and said: "I know truly that this commandery does not match your merit and standing — but the times are not yet settled, and I need you to hold and soothe the region.
idiomatic: Shizong took his hand and said, "I know Bohai is beneath your deserts — but the realm is not yet secure, and I need you to hold the coast steady.

literal: Besides, to ride in brocade by day — the ancients prized this. Govern well, calm the sea's edge — no need to study how ordinary prefects attend the provincial seat.
idiomatic: Besides, to ride home in brocade by daylight — the ancients thought it the highest honor. Take command, calm the seaboard; do not trouble yourself with the petty routine of an ordinary prefect reporting to the provincial capital.

literal: He was also permitted to gather a personal following of a thousand men.
idiomatic: He was also allowed to muster a personal guard of a thousand men.

literal: Later his rank was advanced one grade and Fast-Cavalry General was added.
idiomatic: Later his rank was raised one step and he was named general of fast cavalry.

literal: In the second year of Tianbao he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: In Tianbao 2 he was made chief administrator to the grand commandant.

literal: In the third year, repeatedly acting in Southern Qing Province affairs at his present rank.
idiomatic: In the third year he repeatedly acted as chief of Southern Qing Province while keeping his existing rank.

literal: In the fourth year, on account of an offense he was dismissed.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he was dismissed for an offense.
